hints: All measurable amounts are multiples of gcd(a,b).
Container A cannot hold more than its capacity.
These two conditions are also sufficient.
analogy: The two capacities generate every nonnegative multiple of their greatest common divisor up to either container?s capacity.
example: For capacities 5 and 3, gcd is 1 and 4<=5, so the answer is YES. For capacities 2 and 2, one unit is impossible.
algorithm: For each query compute g=gcd(a,b) using Euclid?s algorithm. Print YES exactly when x<=a and x is divisible by g; otherwise print NO.
correctness: Filling, emptying and pouring preserve the property that both amounts are multiples of g, and A cannot exceed a. Conversely, the standard repeated-fill-and-pour construction generates every multiple of g between zero and a in container A, so both conditions are sufficient.
complexity: Each query takes O(log(min(a,b))) time and O(1) extra space.
